knowledges.content: Solution-processable organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites have the general formula CH3NH3PbX3 where X = Cl, Br, or I, and have attracted attention as light-harvesting materials for mesoscopic solar cells [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: perovskite_definition
knowledges.title: Perovskite material definition

knowledges.content: The single-step deposition of perovskite pigment onto mesoporous metal oxide films using a mixture of PbX2 and CH3NH3X in a common solvent produces large morphological variations, resulting in a wide spread of photovoltaic performance in the resulting devices [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: prior_work_limitation
knowledges.title: Single-step deposition produces morphological variability

knowledges.content: A sequential deposition method is introduced for the formation of the perovskite pigment within the porous metal oxide film: PbI2 is first introduced from solution into a nanoporous titanium dioxide film and subsequently transformed into the perovskite by exposing it to a solution of CH3NH3I [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: sequential_deposition_introduced

metadata.prior_justification: Core method clearly described in paper.

knowledges.title: Sequential deposition method introduced

knowledges.content: The sequential deposition method permits much better control over perovskite morphology than the previously employed single-step route [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: control_improvement
knowledges.title: Sequential method improves morphology control

knowledges.content: Using the sequential deposition technique for solid-state mesoscopic solar cells, a power conversion efficiency of approximately 15% is achieved under standard AM1.5G test conditions [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: efficiency_achieved
knowledges.title: 15% efficiency achieved with sequential deposition

knowledges.content: The sequential deposition method greatly increases the reproducibility of photovoltaic performance compared to single-step deposition [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: reproducibility_improvement
knowledges.title: Sequential method improves reproducibility

knowledges.content: The photovoltaic device structure consists of: FTO-coated glass substrate (front contact), 30-40 nm TiO2 compact layer (aerosol spray pyrolysis), 350 nm mesoporous TiO2 layer (20-nm-sized anatase particles), perovskite infiltrant, spiro-MeOTAD hole-transporting material (HTM), and 80 nm Au back contact [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: device_structure
knowledges.title: Device structure configuration

knowledges.content: Mesoporous TiO2 films composed of 20-nm-sized particles are deposited by spin coating at 5,000 rpm for 30 s using TiO2 paste (Dyesol 18NRT) diluted in ethanol (2:7 weight ratio), followed by drying at 125 C and annealing at 500 C for 15 min [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: mesoporous_tio2_deposition
knowledges.title: Mesoporous TiO2 deposition protocol

knowledges.content: PbI2 is dissolved in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) at a concentration of 462 mg/ml (~1 M) under stirring at 70 C. The mesoporous TiO2 films are infiltrated by spin coating at 6,500 rpm for 90 s, then dried at 70 C for 30 min [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: pbi2_infiltration
knowledges.title: PbI2 infiltration protocol

knowledges.content: After PbI2 infiltration, films are dipped in a solution of CH3NH3I in 2-propanol (10 mg/ml) for 20 s, rinsed with 2-propanol, and dried at 70 C for 30 min to convert PbI2 to CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: mai_conversion
knowledges.title: Methylammonium iodide conversion protocol

knowledges.content: The HTM is deposited by spin coating at 4,000 rpm for 30 s using a solution of spiro-MeOTAD (72.3 mg), 4-tert-butylpyridine (28.8 ul), lithium bis(trifluoromethylsulphonyl)imide (17.5 ul of 520 mg/ml in acetonitrile), and Co(III) dopant (29 ul of 300 mg/ml in acetonitrile) in 1 ml chlorobenzene [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: htm_deposition
knowledges.title: HTM spin-coating formulation

knowledges.content: For the best-performing devices (15% PCE), the PbI2 is spin-cast at 6,500 rpm for 5 s (instead of 90 s), and samples are pre-wetted by dipping in 2-propanol for 1-2 s before the CH3NH3I conversion step [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: best_device_modification

metadata.prior_justification: Direct description of modified conditions: shorter spin-cast and pre-wetting.

knowledges.title: Modified conditions for best-performing devices

knowledges.content: Current-voltage characteristics are measured under simulated AM1.5G solar irradiation using a 450 W xenon lamp with Schott K113 Tempax sunlight filter. Light intensity is calibrated using a calibrated Si reference diode with KG-3 infrared cut-off filter. Devices are measured using a 0.285 cm^2 metal aperture [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: j_v_measurement
knowledges.title: J-V characterization method

knowledges.content: IPCE spectra are recorded as functions of wavelength under constant white light bias (approximately 5 mW/cm^2) from an array of white LEDs. The excitation beam from a 300 W xenon lamp is focused through a Gemini-180 double monochromator and chopped at approximately 2 Hz, detected with an SR830 DSP Lock-In Amplifier [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: ipce_measurement
knowledges.title: IPCE measurement method

knowledges.content: For long-term stability tests, devices are sealed in argon using a 50-mm-thick hot-melting polymer and microscope coverslip. Devices are subjected to constant light soaking at approximately 100 mW/cm^2 using white LED array (Philips LXM3-PW51 4000K), maintained at maximum power point, at approximately 45 C. J-V measurements at different light intensities are recorded automatically every 2 h [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: stability_testing
knowledges.title: Long-term stability test protocol

knowledges.content: Optical absorption measurements are carried out using a Varian Cary 5 spectrophotometer. Photoluminescence is measured on a Horiba Jobin Yvon Fluorolog spectrofluorometer. Samples are placed vertically in a 10 mm path length cuvette [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: optical_spectroscopy
knowledges.title: Optical spectroscopy methods

knowledges.content: X-ray powder diagrams are recorded on an X'Pert MPD PRO (PANalytical) with Cu anode (lambda = 1.54060 A), graphite (002) monochromator, and RTMS X'Celerator detector in BRAGG-BRENTANO geometry. Step size is 0.008 deg with acquisition time up to 7.5 min/deg [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: xrd_measurement
knowledges.title: XRD measurement parameters

knowledges.content: PbI2 infiltration into mesoporous TiO2 films is complete: cross-sectional SEM shows no PbI2 crystals protruding from the surface of the mesoporous anatase layer, indicating the PbI2 is entirely contained within the nanopores of the TiO2 film [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: pbi2_complete_infiltration

metadata.caption: Figure 1a | Cross-sectional SEM of mesoporous TiO2 film infiltrated with PbI2
metadata.prior_justification: Direct SEM observation showing complete PbI2 infiltration into TiO2 nanopores.

knowledges.title: PbI2 completely contained within TiO2 nanopores

knowledges.content: When confined within mesoporous TiO2 scaffold, PbI2 crystal size is limited to approximately 22 nm by the pore size of the host [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: pbi2_crystal_size

metadata.prior_justification: Crystal size (~22 nm) measured from pore size constraint.

knowledges.title: PbI2 crystal size limited to ~22 nm in nanopores

knowledges.content: Dipping the TiO2/PbI2 composite film into CH3NH3I solution (10 mg/ml in 2-propanol) immediately changes its color from yellow to dark brown, indicating formation of CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: color_change_observed
knowledges.title: Color change indicates rapid perovskite formation

knowledges.content: The increase in perovskite absorption at 550 nm during conversion is practically complete within a few seconds of exposing the PbI2-loaded TiO2 film to the CH3NH3I solution. A small additional increase occurring on a timescale of 100 s contributes only a few percent to the total signal and is attributed to morphological changes producing enhanced light scattering [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: absorption_increase

metadata.caption: Figure 1b | Change in absorbance at 550 nm during transformation

knowledges.title: Perovskite absorption increase complete within seconds

knowledges.content: The conversion is accompanied by quenching of PbI2 emission at 425 nm, confirming PbI2 consumption during the reaction with CH3NH3I [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: pl_quenching_pbi2

metadata.caption: Figure 1c | Change in PL intensity at 520 nm during transformation (PbI2 quenching)

knowledges.title: PbI2 photoluminescence quenched during conversion

knowledges.content: The perovskite luminescence at 775 nm increases concomitantly with conversion, passing through a maximum before decreasing to a stationary value due to self-absorption by the perovskite formed during the reaction [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: perovskite_pl_increase

metadata.caption: Figure 1d | Change in PL intensity at 775 nm during transformation

knowledges.title: Perovskite emission at 775 nm increases then decreases

knowledges.content: PbI2 loaded on mesoporous TiO2 shows three additional diffraction peaks (not present for flat glass) that suggest the anatase scaffold induces a different orientation for PbI2 crystal growth, with peaks attributed to the (110) and (111) lattice planes of the 2H polytype and a third peak assigned to a different PbI2 variant [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: pbi2_tio2_orientation

metadata.caption: Figure 1e | XRD spectra showing PbI2 orientation differences

knowledges.title: Mesoporous TiO2 induces different PbI2 crystal orientation

knowledges.content: XRD shows new diffraction peaks after CH3NH3I reaction that are in good agreement with literature data on the tetragonal phase of CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite, confirming complete conversion within the mesoporous TiO2 scaffold [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: perovskite_xrd_confirmed

metadata.prior_justification: Direct XRD measurement showing tetragonal perovskite peaks after conversion.

knowledges.title: Tetragonal perovskite XRD peaks observed after conversion

knowledges.content: On flat glass substrate, conversion of PbI2 to perovskite is incomplete; a large amount of unreacted PbI2 remains even after a dipping time of 45 min, with CH3NH3I insertion hardly proceeding beyond the surface of thin PbI2 films [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: flat_substrate_incomplete_conversion

metadata.prior_justification: Direct XRD observation of unreacted PbI2 after 45 min on flat glass.

knowledges.title: Flat substrate shows incomplete perovskite conversion

knowledges.content: Confining PbI2 crystals to approximately 22 nm within mesoporous TiO2 drastically enhances their rate of conversion to perovskite, completing within a few seconds of contact with methylammonium iodide solution. In contrast, flat surface deposition produces larger 50-200 nm crystallites resulting in incomplete conversion [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: conversion_rate_enhancement
knowledges.title: Nanoscopic confinement dramatically accelerates conversion

knowledges.content: The mesoporous TiO2 scaffold forces the perovskite to adopt a confined nanomorphology dictated by the pore structure [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: nanomorphology_enforced
knowledges.title: Mesoporous scaffold enforces perovskite nanomorphology

knowledges.content: A typical photovoltaic device measured at 95.6 mW/cm^2 shows: short-circuit photocurrent Jsc = 17.1 mA/cm^2, open-circuit voltage Voc = 992 mV, fill factor = 0.73, yielding a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 12.9% [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: typical_device_performance

metadata.caption: Figure 3a | J-V curves for typical photovoltaic device

knowledges.title: Typical device performance: 12.9% PCE

knowledges.content: Statistical data from a batch of ten photovoltaic devices shows an average PCE of 12.0% with a standard deviation of 0.5%, demonstrating high reproducibility [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: device_batch_statistics

metadata.prior_justification: Direct experimental measurement from 10 devices: average PCE 12.0% +/- 0.5%.

knowledges.title: Batch average PCE: 12.0% +/- 0.5%

knowledges.content: IPCE shows photocurrent generation starting at 800 nm, consistent with the bandgap of CH3NH3PbI3 [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: ipce_onset
knowledges.title: IPCE onset at 800 nm matches perovskite bandgap

knowledges.content: IPCE reaches peak values of over 90% in the short-wavelength region of the visible spectrum [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: ipce_peak_value

metadata.caption: Figure 3b | IPCE spectrum
metadata.prior_justification: Direct IPCE measurement showing peak values exceeding 90%.

knowledges.title: IPCE peak exceeds 90% in short wavelengths

knowledges.content: Integrating the overlap of the IPCE spectrum with the AM1.5G solar photon flux yields a current density of 18.4 mA/cm^2, in excellent agreement with the measured photocurrent density extrapolated to 17.9 mA/cm^2 at standard AM1.5G intensity of 100 mW/cm^2. This confirms negligible mismatch between simulated sunlight and AM1.5G standard [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: integrated_current_match
knowledges.title: Integrated IPCE current matches measured Jsc

knowledges.content: The low IPCE values in the 600-800 nm range result from the smaller absorption of the perovskite in this spectral region, as shown by the light-harvesting efficiency (LHE) spectrum [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: lhe_data
knowledges.title: Low IPCE in 600-800 nm due to reduced light harvesting

knowledges.content: The absorbed-photon-to-current conversion efficiency (APCE) derived from IPCE and LHE is greater than 90% over the whole visible region (without correction for reflective losses), indicating near-unity quantum yield for charge carrier generation and collection [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: apce_exceeds_90_percent

metadata.caption: Figure 3d | APCE spectrum
metadata.prior_justification: Direct measurement showing APCE >90% across visible range without correction for reflective losses.

knowledges.title: APCE exceeds 90% indicating near-unity quantum yield

knowledges.content: The best-performing cell (fabricated with modified conditions) shows: Jsc = 20.0 mA/cm^2, Voc = 993 mV, fill factor = 0.73, yielding a PCE of 15.0% measured at 96.4 mW/cm^2. Several cells achieved PCEs between 14% and 15% [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: best_device_performance

metadata.caption: Figure 3e | J-V curves for best-performing cell

knowledges.title: Best device: 15.0% PCE

knowledges.content: One of the best-performing devices was sent to an accredited photovoltaic calibration laboratory for certification, confirming a power conversion efficiency of 14.14% under standard AM1.5G reporting conditions [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: certified_efficiency
knowledges.title: Certified PCE: 14.14%

knowledges.content: The significantly higher photocurrent in top-performance devices is attributed to increased loading of the porous TiO2 film with perovskite pigment and increased light scattering from the pre-wetting step, improving the long-wavelength response of the cell [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: best_device_improvement_attributed

metadata.prior_justification: Attribution supported by pre-wetting modification and spectral response changes.

knowledges.title: Higher photocurrent from increased loading and light scattering

knowledges.content: A sealed photovoltaic device maintained more than 80% of its initial PCE after 500 hours of continuous light soaking at approximately 100 mW/cm^2 and 45 C under argon atmosphere with maximum power point tracking [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: stability_result

metadata.prior_justification: Direct 500-hour stability test: device retains >80% of initial PCE.

knowledges.title: Device retains >80% PCE after 500 hours

knowledges.content: No change in short-circuit photocurrent is observed during the 500-hour stability test, indicating no photodegradation of the perovskite light harvester [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: no_photodegradation

metadata.prior_justification: Direct observation of unchanged Jsc during stability test.

knowledges.title: No photodegradation observed

knowledges.content: The decrease in PCE during stability testing is due only to decreases in open-circuit voltage and fill factor, with similar decay shapes suggesting a linked degradation mechanism attributed mainly to a decrease in shunt resistance [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: pce_decrease_mechanism
knowledges.title: PCE decrease due to Voc and FF reduction from shunt resistance loss

knowledges.content: The confinement of PbI2 within the nanoporous TiO2 network greatly facilitates its conversion to the perovskite pigment, compared to flat substrate deposition [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: conversion_facilitation
knowledges.title: Nanoporous confinement facilitates perovskite conversion

knowledges.content: The mesoporous scaffold forces the perovskite to adopt a confined nanomorphology [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: nanomorphology_enforcement
knowledges.title: Mesoporous scaffold enforces perovskite nanomorphology

knowledges.content: The insertion of the organic cation is facilitated through the layered PbI2 structure, which consists of three spatially repeating planes: I-Pb-I. Strong intralayer chemical bonding combined with weak interlayer van der Waals interactions allows easy insertion of guest molecules between the layers [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: layered_pbi2_structure

metadata.prior_justification: Well-established in literature on polytypism and intercalation.

knowledges.title: Layered PbI2 structure enables cation insertion

knowledges.content: The thermodynamic driving force for the two-step conversion is the difference in bulk lattice energy between PbI2 and CH3NH3PbI3, with the initial crystal lattice serving as a template for the formation of the desired compound. This is analogous to ion exchange reactions used to convert II-V semiconductor nanocrystals to III-V analogues while preserving particle size and distribution [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: thermodynamic_driving_force

metadata.prior_justification: Established principle from semiconductor nanocrystal ion exchange literature.

knowledges.title: Lattice energy difference drives conversion

knowledges.content: The large energy of formation of the hybrid perovskite combined with the nanoscopic morphology of the PbI2 precursor (approximately 22 nm crystals) greatly enhances reaction kinetics, enabling complete transformation within seconds of contact with methylammonium iodide solution [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: reaction_kinetics_enhancement

metadata.prior_justification: Reasonable mechanistic interpretation combining formation energy and nanoscale morphology.

knowledges.title: Nanoscopic morphology combined with high formation energy enhances kinetics

knowledges.content: The two-step sequential deposition method is applicable to other preformed metal halide mesostructures that can be converted into the desired perovskite by insertion reactions [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: two_step_method_applicability
knowledges.title: Sequential deposition applicable to other metal halide mesostructures

knowledges.content: The power conversion efficiency of 15% achieved with the best device is amongst the highest for solution-processed photovoltaics and sets a new record for organic or hybrid inorganic-organic solar cells at the time of publication [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: record_efficiency
knowledges.title: 15% PCE sets record for solution-processed photovoltaics

knowledges.content: The sequential deposition method provides a means to achieve excellent photovoltaic performance with high reproducibility, addressing the wide spread of performance characteristic of single-step deposition methods [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: reproducibility_demonstrated
knowledges.title: Method enables reproducible high performance

knowledges.content: Perovskite-based photovoltaic devices fabricated using this method have potential for widespread application and may eventually rival conventional silicon-based photovoltaics [@Burschka2013].
knowledges.label: future_potential
knowledges.title: Perovskite photovoltaics may rival silicon

module_titles.motivation: Burschka2013: Sequential deposition as a route to high-performance perovskite-sensitized solar cells.

metadata.reason: The sequential method infiltrates PbI2 into TiO2 nanopores first, then converts in place. This prevents uncontrolled precipitation that causes morphological variations in single-step deposition (@prior_work_limitation). The complete infiltration shown by SEM confirms uniform loading within the porous structure.

The 22 nm crystal size confined in TiO2 pores converts completely within seconds (@perovskite_xrd_confirmed), while flat substrates with 50-200 nm crystallites show incomplete conversion even after 45 min (@flat_substrate_incomplete_conversion). This demonstrates that nanoscopic confinement drastically accelerates conversion.

Better morphology control (@control_improvement) and rapid complete conversion (@conversion_rate_enhancement) produce uniform perovskite films with optimal light harvesting and charge collection, enabling the reported 15% PCE. The certified 14.14% (@certified_efficiency) confirms this performance.

The batch average of 12.0% with standard deviation of only 0.5% (@device_batch_statistics) demonstrates excellent reproducibility. This stems from the controlled morphology (@control_improvement) that eliminates the wide performance spread seen in single-step deposition.

The modified conditions (shorter spin-cast time and pre-wetting) increase perovskite loading in the TiO2 pores and enhance light scattering (@best_device_improvement_attributed). This produces the higher Jsc of 20.0 mA/cm^2 and 15.0% PCE (@best_device_performance).

After 500 hours of light soaking, the device retains >80% PCE (@stability_result) with no change in Jsc (@no_photodegradation), confirming the perovskite is stable. The PCE decrease is attributed to shunt resistance loss affecting Voc and FF, not to light harvester degradation.

The layered I-Pb-I structure of PbI2 (@layered_pbi2_structure) allows easy cation insertion between layers. The large lattice energy difference (@thermodynamic_driving_force) provides the driving force, and the 22 nm crystal size (@reaction_kinetics_enhancement) greatly enhances kinetics, together explaining the rapid complete conversion.

Peak IPCE >90% (@ipce_peak_value) and APCE >90% across visible range (@apce_exceeds_90_percent) demonstrate near-unity quantum yield for carrier generation and collection. This explains why the integrated current (18.4 mA/cm^2) matches the measured Jsc.
